problem: Do two swapped subsets of the same instrument require target labels, or can earlier paired reference exposures maintain the original model after replacing sensors? The A/B test labels and previous transfer outcomes are already known. This is an added-information branch tested on held-out dates; upstream 13-date file measured both banks simultaneously. Practical use requires a known physical channel mapping and recordings from both old and spare sensors before installation.
split: Exact unchanged three development dates and all ten subsequent evaluation dates, both A->B and B->A as well as A->A and B->B controls, same three FIGARO channels, concentration labels, seed grid and delayed 32/date feedback. Reference fit uses 300 paired readings on source dates with no labels from later dates. Never read old channels at service time. Old-device training, paired measurement counts and extra CPU cost are explicit.
transforms: Register identity, per-channel least-squares affine direct standardization spare->old using paired source measurements, and full three-channel ridge with standardized input/output, alpha 1, same 300 pairs. This is adaptation of direct standardization from instrument calibration transfer. Compare source/field feature standardization and matched-model performance to identity. For a narrow diagnostic include a negative control permuting the paired reference row by a deterministic nonzero shift of half the source records; do not promote the sham. Always-source logistic, always mixed retrain, always local retrain and ongoing recipe selection reuse exact prior SiteTraining models, original y and all service batches. All mapped candidates have the same reference cost; identity with identical information also competes.
autonomy: One predeployment decision uses only known reference pairs: hold out complete source dates in turn; for identity/diagonal/full mapping, fit transforms on other days, compute date-equal mean of feature reconstruction squared errors normalized by training old-channel variance on held date. Choose best mean; break ties identity then diagonal then full; refit mapping on all pairs. Also a fixed full mapping and fixed identity, avoiding retrospective best-map labeling. A second control fits full transform only from first source date; compare benefit of more reference pairs. Report case with calibration present and normal mode with no spare reference pairs separately. Site-time decisions use only prior returned labels. Test first with seed 17, also all 13 existing draws for auto, identity and fixed full. No use of pair information for sites without real paired sensors.
adoption: At least .01 Macro-F1 improvement versus strongest no-pair baseline on both directions, worst-class recall decrease <=.02, same-subset controls protected; compare realized scores also to fixed mapped tools. If contribution is entirely from fixed calibration state that explicitly. This experiment alone cannot promote an official default lacking paired calibrations.
